official_measurement_examples.name: Parks and gardens collection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 1,723 historic parks and gardens with collector activity on 24 July 2026; registration is a designated heritage asset consideration rather than a separate general development-consent regime.

official_measurement_examples.name: Park grades
official_measurement_examples.fact: Registered parks and gardens use Grades I, II* and II; grade is heritage significance context and must not be converted directly into an automatic parcel refusal score.

official_measurement_examples.name: Battlefield record-count distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data shows 94 battlefield records while Historic England states that 47 battlefields are on the Register, so dataset record count must not be treated as a unique-site count without reconciliation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Battlefield consent distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England states registered battlefields do not have a separate battlefield consent regime; their significance is considered through planning and other applicable controls.

official_measurement_examples.name: World Heritage statutory-control distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data notes that UNESCO World Heritage designation brings no additional statutory controls by itself, although World Heritage Sites are designated heritage assets protected through planning and overlapping designations.

official_measurement_examples.name: World Heritage buffer zones
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data separately records World Heritage Site buffer zones, so a buffer polygon must not be treated as the core World Heritage Site designation itself.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current Historic England GIS
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England's designation downloads list parks and gardens, battlefields and World Heritage Sites as updated on 14 July 2026, so older cached geometries must retain version context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Significance assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Heritage designation identifies significance and policy weight but does not by itself determine land ownership, access rights, development capacity or the final planning balance.

core_rules: registered park and garden is a designated heritage asset not a parcel score
park grade must remain separate from planning outcome
battlefield dataset record count is not necessarily unique battlefield count
registered battlefield has no separate general battlefield consent regime
battlefield registration does not prove public access
World Heritage Site designation is distinct from overlapping statutory designations
World Heritage designation alone does not create an additional standalone statutory consent
World Heritage buffer zone is distinct from core site geometry
Historic England current GIS version must be retained
heritage significance requires proposal-specific impact assessment
designation does not determine land ownership
heritage protection does not itself reserve or remove infrastructure capacity
heritage-at-risk status is distinct from designation existence
absence from one national derivative collection is not definitive absence from NHLE
no parcel heritage clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
